name: Omar Novak

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing or campaign for a side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a normal day at the contact centre.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43, finished secondary school, and have answered calls and chats here for years. I know the usual billing cases and do about as well as the other experienced agents. The evening rota supplement puts my pay above the usual rate, though I am not a lead. I use AI for a draft now and then, after someone has tested it, and read the account before sending.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What happens after the evening shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Ada and I have two children in school and a mortgage. Ada works at a community library, and we have around nine months of expenses saved. Plenty of other centres are nearby, but I would rather fix a problem at this one than switch badges for the sake of it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor a draft that saves a minute is useful only if the bill amount is right. I would ask agents to compare any suggested credit with the account history.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my evening shifts and pay to continue. Nine months saved means a broken appliance or a missed library shift will not shake the mortgage. I still care whether the centre raises targets, but that is not an immediate income fear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep the evening billing calls and check the occasional AI draft against the account. I would put a fixed part of the rota supplement into our reserve. In the first year I would keep our family plans on the same budget and take a wrong draft to a normal team discussion.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job and household in this picture. I would be irritated by careless drafts, not frightened by them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the last bad draft miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A promised credit had not yet been approved. The AI draft wrote as if the money was already back, so I checked the approval line before calling the customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Ada want you to change jobs for a better tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Ada would ask what the hours and wage are, and whether I would still be home for the children on my days off.

I would ask agents to check **credits** against account history.
think: I expect my **evening pay** to continue through this mild change.
Our nine-month **reserve** protects ordinary household surprises without threatening the mortgage.
do: Keep answering **billing calls** and checking drafts.
Discuss a wrong **credit draft** with my team.
S0.quote: The AI draft wrote as if the money was already back, so I checked the approval line before calling the customer.
fieldNote: His higher pay comes from **evening hours**, not a lead role.
He uses AI **occasionally** after others test it.
A nine-month reserve gives the household real **room**.

steps.text: Keep taking evening billing calls and check AI drafts against account history
Save a fixed part of the evening rota supplement

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues the easy chats may leave first, and we should see paid-hour figures before praising the savings. I would join the union meeting to ask for a fair route into the cases people still handle.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the centre could cut evening seats even if it keeps difficult calls. I could lose the evening shift supplement that makes our pay comfortable. We have nine months saved and many nearby centres, but a new opening might pay less for shorter hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would trial the new answer checker on paid time if offered and record wrong billing credits. I would join the union meeting with evening-hour figures and ask for funded training tied to posted jobs. In the first year, if my hours fall I would apply only to posted paid review roles whose written wages and hours cover our mortgage; I would stay until a real offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing the evening premium, though I have time to compare offers. My reserve lets me speak up without pretending my job is guaranteed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask a new employer first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The full weekly wage after the evening supplement is gone, not just the hourly rate. I would also ask whether the hours leave Ada and me a workable school pickup plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you enrol in training now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would complete a short review course only if a posted paid vacancy required it and the employer funded both the fee and study hours. I would not buy a speculative course from our reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor AGI by 2028 could take the calls and checks we now do. I would ask the union to seek written notice and named paid jobs before the evening rota disappears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my headset work could end in 2028, before robots arrive around 2031. Nine months saved gives us a search window, but several nearby centres might stop hiring together. Ada's library wage would not replace mine for long against the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would join the union request for written notice and keep our reserve liquid for the mortgage. I would check actual paid review vacancies each week and take a funded course on paid time only if a named posted role requires it. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if my post ends I would apply for a paid review opening only if written wages and hours cover the mortgage and school pickup; I would not leave before a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious rather than helpless. Nine months of expenses saved is real time to search, even if the whole occupation is changing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family for a job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only with a signed offer whose wage covers the new housing and travel costs, and a school route that works for both children. We can search nearby first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the evening rota may change and our routines might too. I would not make them worry about a date on a card before any written notice arrives.

say: I would seek **written notice** through the union.
I would ask for named **paid jobs** before evening cuts.
think: My headset job could end in **2028**.

do: Join the **union request** for notice now.

fieldNote: He distinguishes 2028 screen work from later **robots**.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team five years lets us ask whether the new review jobs have real wages and duties. I would keep the union involved so people on every rota see the terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect full AGI in 2031 to take most calls, but I could learn account appeals before then. I have nine months saved and plenty of nearby centres to compare. Robots around 2034 are later than the thinking work on my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would ask for a paid trial in account appeals and record the disputed bills I help settle. I would join union meetings on posted review roles and take a funded appeals course on paid time only if an actual paid vacancy requires it. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if calls end I would apply only to jobs whose written wages and hours cover our mortgage and school pickup, staying until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy, because a route exists but its future is uncertain. Five years makes checking the job possible without spending our reserve on guesses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the paid trial useful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A posted job description, a real dispute to work through and the wage for the role. A demonstration without a real dispute would keep me on the evening shift. I would ask again later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a lower wage to avoid the queue?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not if it makes the mortgage or pickup unworkable. Ada and I would compare the whole week, including travel and child care.

fieldNote: He needs an actual **dispute**, not a demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues a decade is long enough to build a fair paid route into other work. I would ask the union to compare staff hours and posted wages every year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 when AGI arrives in 2036, and we might still owe the mortgage. I could spend those years learning appeals, but I will not assume any desk survives full AGI. Robots around 2039 come after the screen change for our work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep taking evening calls and put part of the supplement into savings. I would ask for one paid appeals shift each month if the centre offers a real opening, and attend annual union meetings on hours and wages. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if calls end I would apply for a posted paid review role only if written wages and hours cover the mortgage and the children’s school routine; I would leave only after signing an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about 2036, but calm enough about the next few years. A decade gives me time to test a paid role without burning the reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you set a retirement date now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I do not know the mortgage balance in 2036, and I have not counted on stopping work at 53. I would plan around paid jobs I can see.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the appeals shift is unpaid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the evening rota and learn from the calls already assigned to me. I will not swap a paid evening call shift for an unpaid appeals trial.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Nine months saved gives us time, but it cannot make the nearby centres keep hiring. Written notice, a paid review vacancy with wages and hours that protect the mortgage and school pickup, and funded study time would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether an agent can still correct a disputed credit when the answer comes from a machine. A wrong number needs a person with authority, not just a polite apology.

headlineQuote: A wrong number needs a person with authority, not just a polite apology.
portrait: Omar is a **43-year-old experienced** contact centre agent with secondary school education and average skill.
His evening supplement raises his **pay**, and he has nine months saved with Ada against a mortgage.
He uses AI **occasionally** after it proves useful, and has plenty of nearby job options.
He joins **union meetings** for notice and posted routes that preserve wages and school pickup.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his headset work while nearby centres stop hiring together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a paid review vacancy with mortgage-covering wages and pickup-compatible hours, and funded study time would help.
